title: Does the view fit?
hints: Two conditions, both needed: the start isn't negative, and the end isn't past `n`. The end is one past the last element, so `off + k == n` still fits.
Try `off = INT_MAX`, `k = 2`. What is `off + k` in C? (The runner traps undefined behavior, so if your code overflows, that test crashes.)
Signed overflow is undefined. Move `k` to the other side: `off <= n - k`. With these inputs `n - k` can't overflow, and when `k > n` it's negative, so the check still says no.
explain: The solution returns `off >= 0 && off <= n - k`. Writing it as `off <= n - k` instead of `off + k <= n` avoids signed overflow when `off` is huge. Overflow is undefined behavior in C: an optimizer may quietly compute the "right" answer, so the naive check can look fine at -O1. The exercise runner compiles with `-fsanitize=undefined -fsanitize-trap=undefined` (the same as the render grader), so the naive version crashes on the INT_MAX test instead of passing by luck.
